subject: Echo widget — instant playback via paragraph-chunk TTS

problem.symptom: User reported 10–30 second wait after clicking Play on the OpenAI BYOK path. Audio did not begin until the entire page was synthesized.
problem.root_cause: Two compounding parameters. (1) groupIntoBatches() used MAX = 3000 chars, so the first batch covered roughly the entire opening section of a typical page. (2) fetchBatchAudio() used model 'tts-1-hd', which is ~3x slower than 'tts-1'. A 3000-char batch on HD takes 10–20s round-trip on a typical connection. The architecture was already correct — per-paragraph chunking with parallel prefetch — but the batch size and model choice negated it.

change_1.rationale: 500-char batches keep each TTS round-trip under ~1.5s. MIN_FLOOR prevents single-word batches from short headings — items shorter than 200 chars are coalesced into their neighbour before flushing.

change_2.rationale: tts-1 is ~3x faster. At 500-char batch sizes the quality difference is imperceptible on most speakers or earbuds. The user explicitly chose latency — this delivers it.

change_3.after: nextPromise + nextNextPromise (prefetch i+1 and i+2); pipeline advances to i+3 on each chunk.ended
change_3.rationale: Deeper lookahead ensures the buffer is never empty even on a slightly slow network. Concurrency cap remains 2 in-flight beyond the current chunk.

change_4.before: no cancel() before speak(); no voices guard
change_4.after: speechSynthesis.cancel() before first speak(); rAF-loop waits for voices to load before speaking
change_4.rationale: Safari and iOS can have a stuck utterance queue from a prior page. cancel() clears it. The rAF poll resolves the common Safari issue where voices array is empty at first click.

latency_budget.target: First audio playing within 1.5s of click
latency_budget.math: 500 chars / 4 ≈ 125 tokens × ~30ms/token generation + ~200ms network round-trip ≈ 1.0s typical
latency_budget.worst_case: 600-char batch (floor cap) ≈ 150 tokens × 30ms + 200ms ≈ 1.25s — still within target
latency_budget.previous: 3000-char batch on tts-1-hd ≈ 750 tokens × 90ms + 200ms ≈ 68s worst case; measured user experience was 10–30s

verification_plan.short_page: Briefing 017 (~2k words) — expected: first chunk plays in <1.5s; ~4–6 total batches
verification_plan.medium_page: Cordova customer note — expected: first chunk plays in <1.5s; ~8–12 total batches
verification_plan.long_page: /research/people-graph-360.html (~6400 words) — expected: first chunk plays in <1.5s; ~20–30 total batches; buffer stays ahead throughout
verification_plan.browser_free: Open panel, select Browser engine, click Play — should begin speaking immediately without the stuck-queue Safari regression

open_issues: tts-1 vs tts-1-hd toggle is not yet exposed in the UI. If fidelity matters more than latency for a specific use (podcast recording, conference demo), a settings option could switch chunks 2+ to HD after the first paragraph plays. Deferred — not needed for the primary complaint.

The rAF-loop voices guard introduces a theoretical infinite loop if speechSynthesis.getVoices() never populates (e.g., a browser with TTS disabled). In practice this matches prior behaviour (speak() would silently fail); documented here for completeness.
no_changes: Widget UI — visual design unchanged. Tessera owns that surface.
BYOK key handling — key stays in localStorage, never leaves the browser.
